title: Integrating RNA-Seq and AI-derived Digital Pathomics for Multimodal Survival Prediction in Oral Cancer
text:
Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is a life-threatening disease with poor survival rates; however, there are
no reliable mortality risk markers to determine individual risk in patients within the same cancer stage. This study
aims to develop and validate a novel OSCC mortality risk score integrating RNA sequencing (RNA-Seq) data,
digital pathomic features, with clinicopathologic data to predict 2-year cancer-specific survival. Additionally, we
will evaluate the clinical utility of brush swabs rather than tissue biopsies to perform RNA-Seq, aiming to establish
a noninvasive workflow for predicting mortality risk at the time of diagnosis.

title: Genetics
text: PROJECT SUMMARY—Genetics Core (Core F) Mendelian mutations, common risk factors, and – more recently – rare risk-associated variants have been identified in neurodegenerative diseases. Yet, a significant proportion of the heritability for Alzheimer's disease (AD) and frontotemporal dementia (FTD) remains unexplained, suggesting that additional genetic risk factors await identification. This PPG Genetics Core has supported PPG investigators over the past ൭൫ years by ൬) collecting and storing DNA and RNA samples from the entire PPG cohort; ൭) providing genetic testing for known pathogenic causes of dementia and risk-associated variants, using both traditional and next-generation sequencing methods; ൮) contributing to the discovery of novel genes and novel risk-associated variants through data generation and case-based screening, using genetic and genomic approaches; and ൯) establishing an informatics platform to facilitate data sharing, storage, and mining, including access to dedicated computational and storage resources. In this renewal application, we propose to leverage this infrastructure and expertise to expand the portfolio of genetic and genomics assays available to the PPG. In the context of expanding roles, we propose to transition primary core activities from UCLA (Geschwind) to UCSF (Yokoyama). We will continue sample collection and banking and will expand our sequencing and genotyping efforts to include whole exome sequencing for gene screening, genome-wide SNP arrays for population mapping, fragment analysis for disease- causing trinucleotide repeat expansions, and transcriptomics in support of Project ൭: Molecular Biomarkers. Such data will be integrated with the clinical, imaging, biomarker, and neuropathological studies being conducted within the PPG to advance our understanding of the genetic architecture of neurodegenerative disease. Given the fundamental nature of genetic information in the etiology and pathophysiology of FTD, this core serves all the projects in this program and is linked to the other PPG cores.

title: Understanding regulation of pediatric regenerative myogenesis and its implication for muscle disease
text:
Skeletal muscle regeneration requires coordinated actions of muscle stem cells and a multitude of muscle-
resident cell types that regulate the stem cell niche. We have identified immune and stromal components of the
muscle niche differentially modulate the efficiency of the muscle stem cell response in pediatric and adult
muscle, which is altered in the context of degenerative pediatric muscle diseases. The work in this proposal will
decipher how the muscle niche promotes efficient regeneration and how alteration in this in pediatric-onset
degenerative muscle wasting diseases, such as Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy, contributes to disease
progression and severity.

title: Center for Human Health and the Environment (CHHE)
text:
The Center for Human Health and the Environment (CHHE) serves as the concentrated point of translational
environmental health science research for NC State and its partner universities (ECU and NCCU), to positively
affect the lives of our combined unique and overlapping community stakeholders. Our multi-disciplinary faculty
implement research with human subjects, genetically modified mice, or alternative models to study exposures,
effects, and specific mechanisms of chemicals impacting our regional communities to better understand how
human health, at both the individual and population level, is impacted by environmental factors. We have used
this knowledge to prevent and/or reduce the adverse impacts of environmental factors on human health, have
built community trust in our science, and have developed communication streams both to and from the CHHE
to inform our future science and decision making.

title: Transcriptional Co-Regulators in Epidermis
text:
Defective epidermal differentiation and barrier formation contributes to a number of skin diseases including
ichthyosis, palmoplantar keratoderma, atopic dermatitis, psoriasis and skin cancer. Understanding the control of
epidermal differentiation will ultimately contribute to our understanding of these skin diseases.

title: Machine Learning-enabled Classification of Extracellular Vesicles Using Nanoplasmonic Microfluidics
text:
Ovarian cancer is a major public health issue and is often diagnosed in later stages, resulting in an
increased risk of death. Extracellular vesicles are nanoscale particles that circulate throughout bodily fluids
and are released by all cells, and their cargo may indicate early signs of ovarian cancer or inform better
treatment strategies. The proposed training and research will create improved methods for characterizing
and classifying extracellular vesicles to improve patient outcomes by developing ultrasensitive detection
devices and machine learning analytical tools.

title: Reversing cancer immunosuppression using attenuated Listeria monocytogenes
text:
Microbial-based cancer therapies have the potential to activate both innate and adaptive arms of the immune
system to promote effective cancer immunotherapy. However, a better understanding of the interactions between
intracellular bacteria and cancer is required to harness the microbe’s full potential. Here we will test our
hypothesis using an attenuated (DactA) strain of Listeria monocytogenes as a therapeutic cancer vaccine that
can act both systemically to promote an adaptive CD8+ T cell response as well as locally within tumors to unleash
CD8+ T cell activity by providing innate immune stimuli that reverses Treg-mediated immunosuppression.

title: Function, evolution and engineering of proteins
text:
The goal of our work is to develop experimental methods to systematically explore the mutational
landscape of biomedically relevant proteins. In the long term, such methods will improve our basic
science understanding of macromolecular function in the cell, clarify the role of genetic variation in
causing disease, and lead to the design biological therapeutics with improved potency and specificity.

title: Improving Adherence to Breast Cancer Treatment Guidelines in Nigeria
text:
This research will assess barriers to guideline-concordant breast cancer care in Nigeria, and methodically
develop and evaluate implementation strategies to promote guideline adoption. The proposed research is
relevant to public health because it aims to improve the evidence-based treatment of breast cancer, the leading
cause of cancer-related death for women in Nigeria. The results of this work will generate fundamental
knowledge and strategies to inform healthcare leaders and policymakers about effective methods to facilitate
adoption of evidence-based cancer care in resource-limited settings, thereby promoting treatment that improves
survival.

title: Recall by Genotype in Diabetes Risk Spectrum
text:
This project will use genetic information from a large healthcare-based biobank to identify adults at especially
high genetic risk for diabetes through distinct pathophysiologic pathways. Participants will be invited for detailed
physiologic testing, including screening for autoimmune diabetes risk and evaluating how people with different
genetic profiles respond to medications, including metformin, a sulfonylurea, and a GLP-1 receptor agonist. The
results will show how genetics can be used to improve personalized prevention and treatment of diabetes.

title: Designing Novel MR Imaging Tools to Quantify Lower-Limb Exercise Adaptations in Knee Osteoarthritis
text:
Knee osteoarthritis is a common and debilitating disease that causes joint pain and eventually leads to joint
replacement surgery but has an unknown cause and no available treatments. Exercising lower-limb muscles is
one of the only recommended options to manage joint pain, but the relationship between the changes in muscle
and the changes in osteoarthritis pain and disease progression are unknown. Thus, we will develop new
magnetic resonance imaging acquisition and analysis techniques of both lower limbs to better understand the
changes that occur in the muscles and the knee during exercise training, with a view towards better future
interventions to manage and treat osteoarthritis.

title: Proteome-wide base editor screens to assess phosphorylation site functionality in immunosenescence
text:
Hundreds to thousands of phosphorylation events in the T cell signaling pathway create dynamic biochemical
networks that orchestrate essentially all functions needed for proper immune responses to malignant cells. We
currently have no technology to functionally screen and identify individual phosphorylation sites that drive
specific, distinct downstream phenotypes. Here, we propose combining DNA base editor-mediated mutations of
phosphorylation sites, proteome-wide, coupled to phenotypic screens to discover novel signaling events that are
associated with defects in T cell effector functions.

title: Exploring autophagy as a cellular response to fusion oncogene-induced stress
text:
Rare cancers often harbor recurrent fusion oncogenes; however, many have not been thoroughly interrogated
to identify their role in tumorigenesis or how they can be targeted to inform patient treatment strategies. I will
characterize the mechanisms by which fusion oncogene expression is restricted to specific cell-types through
autophagy-dependent cell death and determine how conserved this response is. This work will provide insights
into the ways by which fusion oncogene driven proliferation is regulated between cell-types, and explore the
relationship between oncogenic stress, autophagy, and fusion oncogene expression.

title: Measuring Molecular and Mechanical Outcomes of Endoscopic Dilation of Fibrotic Strictures
text:
Understanding the molecular components and mechanical changes in gastrointestinal strictures in response to
balloon or stent dilations is essential for therapeutic decisions in patients with postoperative anastomotic
strictures. This project will longitudinally observe the progression of stricture in an animal model and human
subjects using a clinical endoscope-compatible imaging catheter to develop prognostic criteria for therapeutic
decision-making. Successful completion of the project will establish the imaging catheter as a valuable tool for
improving the management of strictures and enhancing patient outcomes.

title: Senescent Cells Effects in Response to Pathogens
text:
Individuals with high senescent cell (SenC) accumulation (driven by age or chronic disease) are more susceptible
to morbidity and mortality from infections caused by viral, bacterial, and fungal pathogens than healthier, younger
individuals without a high pre-existing SenC burden. This proposal provides training for the principal investigator
to isolate the role of SenCs as an underlying cause of postinfection morbidity through insights into the biology of
aging and its links to the immune system, exploring sex discrepancies and therefore offering new supplementary
treatment strategies for this vital health concern. The broad and significant translational potential of this
application advances the NIA’s goal of improving the healthspan and well-being of older adults through biological
research that specifically addresses the challenges and needs of this population.

title: Towards a better understanding of the critical role and therapeutic potential of drug resistant genes in multiple myeloma
text:
Multiple myeloma cells frequently become resistant to chemotherapy and immunotherapy, making it difficult
to treat patients with recurring disease. In this project, we will characterize a master regulator of drug-resistant
genes in multiple myeloma. We will also investigate whether a combination therapy targeting tumor cells and
immunosuppressive cells can prevent tumor progression and relapse in myeloma.

title: Canadian Cancer Trials Group - Canadian Collaborating Clinical Trials Network
text:
As the Canadian Collaborating Clinical Trial Network, the Canadian Cancer Trials Group (CCTG) enhances
National Clinical Trials Network (NCTN) capacity to conduct innovative and potentially practice-changing trials.
CCTG’s scientific and regulatory expertise and national network of Canadian researchers contributes strategic
and operational expertise leverages Canadian infrastructure and resources to develop new trial proposals,
increases the pool of potential trial participants for precision medicine, rare cancer, and large definitive trials, and
ensures efficient and effective oversight of NCTN trial conduct in Canada. By facilitating the conduct of trials
that examine questions developed and driven by clinicians and that take advantage of emerging science and new
cancer therapies, patients will have earlier access to new treatments and results will be translated into practice,
policy, and improved cancer outcomes for patients.

title: Multicolor PET to interrogate cancer biology
text:
PROJECT NARRATIVE & PUBLIC HEALTH RELEVANCE STATEMENT
A thorough characterization of a patient’s tumor upfront provides better outcomes, i.e., better insight affords
higher survival rates. In contrast and almost anachronistically, PET imaging (the most sensitive and
quantitative imaging method) is “monochromatic” as it can only assess one parameter at the time, lacking
depth of information. However, the new paradigm of multicolor PET enables quantitative PET acquisitions
of up to four different radiotracers at the same time, allowing us to visualize multiple targets with PET
simultaneously, providing in depth mutiplexed information without increase in dose, time and cost as
exemplified by interrogating the tumor microenvironment and immunotherapies for clinically relevant
signatures.

title: Characterizing and treating peripheral nervous system dysfunction in Sanfilippo Syndrome
text:
Mucopolysaccharidosis Type IIIA, or Sanfilippo Syndrome A, is an inherited disorder where patients develop
severe brain abnormalities and exhibit degeneration in the peripheral nervous system, and there are no approved
therapies. The significance of this work lies in the development of new patient-derived neuronal cell models to
improve our knowledge about the molecular underpinnings of dysfunction in the PNS in Sanfilippo Syndrome to
help elucidate new therapeutic targets for the disease. Additionally, drug candidates identified in these studies
will provide new and accessible treatments for this orphan disease as well as other disorders where heparan
sulfate catabolism goes awry.

title: The next generation of liquid biopsies: Predictive and pharmacologic biomarkers
text:
There is a critical need to better understand the development of resistance to targeted therapies and to identify
new targets for treatment of metastatic prostate cancer. As an integral member of the laboratory of Dr. Joshua
Lang, Dr. Jamie Sperger has developed novel liquid biopsy assays aimed at tackling these questions and they
are now using these tools to monitor the emergence of resistance in prostate cancer to improve our
understanding of cancer, develop new therapeutic interventions and supporting biomarker development.
